what: External single-lab check of three frozen FSRI records on NIST FTT-White cone tests (NIST FTT Dual Cone, 2024) of the polymers that have a NIST MCC card: ABS, HDPE, GPO1 (Glastic, glass-reinforced polyester), GPO3 (Redboard, glass-reinforced polyester), PBT and POM-GF (Delrin 570, 20 wt% glass). That is 12 tests, 6 materials, all at 50 kW/m2, horizontal, spark igniter, no edge frame, no grid. Records: pHRR exp074 (models/v2/phrr_hgb_v4.joblib), TTI exp046 (Poisson GLM, refit on FSRI exactly as the record), FIGRA exp119 (blend b1, refit on FSRI exactly as the record; all its inputs exist on the NIST cards). Each record is used as fitted on FSRI. Nothing is refit on NIST data.
banned_moves_note: (1) Thermal-property join: log_kpc = NaN for every NIST row (NIST has no k or rho*c). No join, no pool change. (2) No material or test is excluded after seeing its influence. The only exclusions are a-priori rules declared here: no MCC card, the FSRI-duplicate rule, and two operator comments that report instrument or recording failures (read with digits masked, before any label). NIST's own outcome-based outlier flags ('... Outlier') are NOT used to exclude anything. (3) FIGRA uses pHRR / t_pHRR from test start, never max HRR(t)/t. (4) STA residue is used only in a label-free unit gate, never as a target or input. (5) No win language, no comparison with any bar (pHRR 0.30, TTI 0.58, FIGRA 0.9724), no 'validated'. population.metadata_dir: Metadata/Prepared-Final/FTT-White/*.json (104 tests, 22 materials; 83 'FTT Cone - NIST' 2018-2020 plus 21 'FTT Dual Cone - NIST' 2024)
population.series_dir: Exp-Data_Prepared-Final/FTT-White/<Testname>.csv, matched to the metadata file by identical stem. A missing or extra file -> BLOCKED.
population.mcc_card_rule: A test enters if Metadata/Materials/<M>.json exists, where <M> is the test's 'Material ID' (exact string, joined on the card FILE STEM), and that card holds exactly one block whose key matches '^<M>_MCC_N2_(\d+)K$' and that block is a non-empty dict with all of: 'Peak HRR (W/g)', 'T_peak (K)', 'T_Onset (K)', 'Heat Of Combustion (kJ/g)', 'Heat Release Capacity (J/gK)', 'Residue Yield (%)'. More than one MCC block for a material -> BLOCKED. The card's own 'Material ID' field is NOT the join key: it is printed and asserted against a known-alias table {POMGF: 'POM-GF'; the other five: equal to the stem}. Any other mismatch -> BLOCKED. (Skeptic fix: the draft joined test 'Material ID' to card 'Material ID'; POMGF tests carry 'POMGF' but the card says 'POM-GF', so the literal rule gives 9 tests / 5 materials and blocks.)
population.not_in_population: HIPS (3 tests; HIPS_MCC_N2_10K is empty), Kydex, PolyIso-1 and XPS-Pink (STA only), PVC, Polycarbonate and XLPE6 (no card blocks), and all 2018-2020 wood tests (cards without MCC). Box (416 NBS legacy tests): no material has an MCC block. data/reviewed (338 MIDAS 2012-2017 tests): no MCC cards and thickness_mm null throughout. No FTT-White 2024 test lives in data/reviewed. Metadata/Parsed/FTT-White/2024 holds pre-review copies of the same 21 tests and is never read.
population.expected: 12 tests / 6 materials: ABS R1; HDPE R1; GPO1 R1, R2; GPO3 R1, R2; PBT R1, R2, R3; POMGF R1, R2, R3. All 'Heat Flux (kW/m2)' 50.0, 'Orientation' Horizontal, 'Ignition Source' Spark Igniter, 'Edge Frame' false, 'Grid' false, 'Separation (mm)' 25.0, 'Institution' 'FTT Dual Cone - NIST', test dates 2024-06-26 to 2024-09-06. MCC rate: 10 K/min for ABS and HDPE; 60 K/min for GPO1, GPO3, PBT and POMGF.

Only got mass data') means no gas was sampled, so oxygen-consumption HRR cannot be computed. This is instrument status, read before any label. The executor asserts that the comment contains 'Sample pump was not on'; else BLOCKED. The specimen was also desiccated more than 24 h (prep field), which is flagged, not excluded.

The operator comment says the recorded ignition time is wrong ('T ignition recorded incorrectly ...'), and its approximate value is never used. test_exclusions.POMGF_Cone_50kW_hor_7mm-Spk-nF-nG_R3: Kept. The comment concerns t_flameout only, which is not used. test_exclusions.missing_inputs: Any test missing Sample Mass, Thickness, Surface Area or Heat Flux, or any material missing a required MCC field, is dropped and counted in summary.json. None is expected.

fsri_duplicate_rule.rule: A cone-db material is excluded as a duplicate of FSRI data in hand if any one holds: (a) its card Manufacturer plus Trade Name names the same product as an FSRI material (FSRI material.json gives no manufacturer, so (a) can only fire through (b) or (c)); (b) any card field (Manufacturer, Trade Name, Distributor / Harvesting Site, Description) or test field (Report Name, Original Source, Sponsor, Sample Description, Specimen Prep) contains, case-insensitively, 'FSRI', 'UL Research', 'Underwriters', 'Materials and Products Database', 'NIJ' or 'JH_'; (c) same polymer class as an FSRI material AND card nominal sheet thickness within 0.3 mm of the FSRI source sheet AND the same supplier. The 7 JH_NIJ materials (Black PMMA, cardboard, FRP, MDF, OSB, white pine, white spruce) belong to the firemodels source, not cone-db; rule (b) would catch any JH_ or NIJ provenance.
fsri_duplicate_rule.expected_result: 0 excluded. Class overlaps that are not duplicates are kept and labelled. 'known class, different product': ABS (King KPC, 6.1-6.3 mm, vs FSRI ABS 3.1 mm sheet); HDPE (Rochling Polystone G, 6.15-6.3 mm, vs FSRI HDPE 3.2 mm; FSRI's HDPE 'alternate names' list includes 'polystone' next to 'hitec', 'playboard' and 'plexar', a synonym list rather than provenance, so rule (a) does not fire, and rule (c) fails on thickness; disclosed as 'possibly the same product line at a different thickness'); GPO1/GPO3 (Haysite glass-reinforced polyester, 6.1-6.6 mm, vs FSRI FRP_Panel 2.3 mm, in all three training sets, and Fiberglass_Skylight, in exp046's training only). 'related class': PBT (an aromatic terephthalate polyester; FSRI PET 6.9 mm and PETG 2.7 mm cast sheets are in all three record training sets). 'new class': POM-GF (no FSRI acetal). The draft labelled PBT 'new class'; the skeptic pass corrected it from the FSRI material list (label-free).
fsri_duplicate_rule.if_any_excluded: Report which rule fired. Then re-check the counts against 'expected'; a mismatch -> BLOCKED.
fsri_duplicate_rule.labels: Three class labels: 'known class, different product' (ABS, HDPE, GPO1, GPO3), 'related class' (PBT), 'new class' (POM-GF). They are fixed here, before scoring.

heating_rate_rule.problem: NIST MCC cards were run at 10 K/min (ABS, HDPE) or 60 K/min (GPO1, GPO3, PBT, POMGF). The FSRI MCC behind the records ran at 30 K/min (0.5 C/s), with one exception: Cotton_Shirt (R1-R3) and Nylon_Carpet_High_Pile (R1-R2) ran at 1 C/s (ingest_fsri_sta_mcc.mcc_self_check). Nylon_Carpet_High_Pile is in exp074's and exp119's training rows, and its mcc_peak_hrr_Wg is the un-normalised material mean (peak_specific_hrr_Wg), as the records were fit. Its mcc_hrc_JgK (exp119) is rate-correct. Peak specific HRR scales with heating rate beta, so the card peak cannot be used as-is.
heating_rate_rule.primary_R1: Lyon's rate normalisation. mcc_peak_hrr_Wg = 'Heat Release Capacity (J/gK)' x 0.5 K/s, i.e. the card HRC (= Q_max/beta, computed by NIST at its measured beta) times FSRI's beta. HRC, h_c ('Heat Of Combustion (kJ/g)', per initial mass) and char yield are carried as-is. The characteristic temperatures 'T_peak (K)' and 'T_Onset (K)' are carried at the native rate, unshifted, because the card gives no kinetic parameter, and shifting them is a second modelling step (see S2).
heating_rate_rule.physics: For single-step first-order pyrolysis at constant heating rate, Q_max = eta_c * beta with eta_c = h_c * E / (e * R * Tp^2). eta_c (the HRC) depends on beta only through Tp^2: a few percent over 10-60 K/min for E ~ 200-500 kJ/mol. To first order, the 30 K/min peak is HRC x 0.5 K/s. h_c and char yield are thermodynamic or stoichiometric and rate-independent to first order. The expected bias of leaving temperatures unshifted: Kissinger shifts of about +9 to +21 K (10 -> 30 K/min) and -8 to -13 K (60 -> 30 K/min), quantified by S2.
heating_rate_rule.citations: Lyon RE, Walters RN. Pyrolysis combustion flow calorimetry. J Anal Appl Pyrolysis 71 (2004) 27-46. ASTM D7309 (MCC; HRC = Q_max/beta, Method A at 1 K/s). Lyon RE, Walters RN, Stoliarov SI. Thermal analysis of flammability. J Therm Anal Calorim 89 (2007) 441-448 (eta_c = h_c E / (e R Tp^2)). Lyon RE. Heat release kinetics. Fire Mater 24 (2000) 179-186. Kissinger HE. Reaction kinetics in differential thermal analysis. Anal Chem 29 (1957) 1702-1706; Akahira T, Sunose T (1971) for the isoconversional form. These were cited from the drafting agent's knowledge and no source was opened this session. The critic checks them.
heating_rate_rule.sensitivity_S1_no_rescaling: Report-only. Card values exactly as reported at the native rate: mcc_peak_hrr_Wg = 'Peak HRR (W/g)', mcc_hrc_JgK = card HRC, temperatures unshifted. Results are reported by MCC-rate stratum (10 K/min: ABS, HDPE; 60 K/min: GPO1, GPO3, PBT, POMGF). This is the plan's 'no rescaling, report both strata separately' option. It shows how much the rate rule matters; it is physically inconsistent with FSRI's 30 K/min inputs by about a factor of 3 (10 K/min) or 0.5 (60 K/min).
heating_rate_rule.sensitivity_S2_single_step_KAS: Report-only. The full single-step correction. E_app = e * R * Tp^2 * HRC / h_c (J/mol; HRC in J/gK, h_c in J/g, Tp in K). Tp' at beta' = 0.5 K/s solves ln(beta'/Tp'^2) + E_app/(R*Tp') = ln(beta/Tp^2) + E_app/(R*Tp) (Kissinger; scipy brentq on [Tp-150, Tp+150]). T_onset' solves the same equation with T_onset in place of Tp (isoconversional KAS form, same E_app). Then mcc_peak_hrr_Wg = HRC * 0.5 * (Tp/Tp')^2 and mcc_hrc_JgK = HRC * (Tp/Tp')^2; mcc_t_peak_C = Tp' - 273.15; mcc_t_onset_C = T_onset' - 273.15. beta = 1/6 K/s for the 10K blocks and 1 K/s for the 60K blocks, from the block name. h_c and char yield are unchanged.
heating_rate_rule.not_done: No PS-anchored or FSRI-anchored scaling: cone-db has no PS MCC run (the PMMA-MaCFP MCC block is empty), and a factor taken from NIST-vs-FSRI or NIST-vs-FAA values would be fitted to this population (banned under 'never').

mcc_from_card.block: <Material ID>_MCC_N2_<r>K in Metadata/Materials/<Material ID>.json. The values are the card's means over 3 runs (4 for GPO3), analogous to the FSRI per-material MCC means. 'Uc ...' fields are never used.
mcc_from_card.mcc_peak_hrr_Wg: primary R1: HRC x 0.5; S1: 'Peak HRR (W/g)'; S2: as above
mcc_from_card.mcc_hrc_JgK (FIGRA only): 'Heat Release Capacity (J/gK)' (primary and S1); S2: HRC x (Tp/Tp')^2
mcc_from_card.mcc_total_hr_kJg: 'Heat Of Combustion (kJ/g)' (h_c per initial mass). It fills exp074's baseline-corrected slot (total_hr_bc_kJg) and exp119's uncorrected slot (total_hr_kJg). NIST's integration and baseline method is not documented at the pin (disclosed).
mcc_from_card.mcc_t_onset_C: 'T_Onset (K)' - 273.15 (S2: KAS-shifted). Definition mismatch, disclosed: FSRI's is T at 5% of baseline-corrected cumulative heat (t_onset_bc_C), and NIST's onset algorithm is not documented at the pin. One value per material serves both exp074 (mean) and exp046 (median). Label-free evidence that the definitions differ (skeptic pass): NIST T_peak - T_Onset is 44 K (ABS), 31 (HDPE), 68 (GPO1), 61 (GPO3), 32 (PBT) and 89 (POM-GF). FSRI t_peak_C - t_onset_bc_C has a median of 105 K (IQR 62-136) over 123 materials: ABS 74, HDPE 35, FRP_Panel 190 (onset 235 C, vs NIST GPO1/GPO3 363/367 C). If NIST's onset sits later than a 5%-of-heat onset, exp046's log_dT is too large, so predicted TTI is biased long, and exp074's mcc_t_onset_C is shifted up. Declared here as a known bias direction. No variant is added and nothing is corrected.
mcc_from_card.mcc_char_yield_pct: 100 x 'Residue Yield (%)'. The MCC block stores a mass fraction despite its label: POM-GF (20 wt% glass) reads 0.2 and the glass-polyester GPOs read 0.6, against STA residues of 17.6, 55.1 and 58.2%. Gate G2 verifies this. The fraction has 1-decimal resolution (+-5 points), which is disclosed.

geometry_G1_primary.rule: Per test, from the test JSON.
geometry_G1_primary.density_kgm3: 'Sample Mass (g)'/1000 / ('Surface Area (m2)' * 'Thickness (mm)'/1000). For the 2024 tests 'Surface Area (m2)' is the 100 x 100 mm specimen face (0.01; 0.01004 for POMGF R1). With no edge frame, exposed area equals planform.
geometry_G1_primary.cone_mass_per_area_kgm2: 'Sample Mass (g)'/1000 / 'Surface Area (m2)' (as the FSRI ingest's SPECIMEN MASS / SURF AREA)
geometry_G1_primary.heat_flux_kWm2: 'Heat Flux (kW/m2)'; assert equal to the Testname token ('50kW')

features.geometry_G2_S3: Report-only. Per material, the median of the G1 thickness, density and mass/area over that material's tests in the population (all 12 tests, independent of target exclusions), applied to each of its rows. This mirrors the material-level FSRI training features.
features.log_kpc: NaN for every row and variant. exp074's HGB routes NaN natively. exp046's SimpleImputer(median, add_indicator=True) fills the FSRI training median and sets the indicator; assert that the fitted imputer carries an indicator for log_kpc. exp119 does not use it.
features.tti_phys: exp046 inputs per test, as train_tti_v5_physics builds them: log_q = log(1e3 * heat_flux_kWm2); log_dT = log(mcc_t_onset_C - 20); log_kpc = NaN; log_L = log(cone_thickness_mm / 1000); log_rho = log(density_kgm3). Column order [log_q, log_dT, log_kpc, log_L, log_rho] (v5.PHYS).
features.exp074_columns: [heat_flux_kWm2, mcc_peak_hrr_Wg, mcc_char_yield_pct, cone_mass_per_area_kgm2, cone_thickness_mm, density_kgm3, mcc_total_hr_kJg, mcc_t_peak_C, mcc_t_onset_C, log_kpc]
features.exp119_columns: [heat_flux_kWm2, mcc_peak_hrr_Wg, mcc_char_yield_pct, density_kgm3, cone_thickness_mm, cone_mass_per_area_kgm2, mcc_hrc_JgK, mcc_total_hr_kJg, mcc_t_peak_C]
features.extrapolation_flags: Label-free and report-only. For every row and variant, list each input outside the [min, max] of that record's FSRI training rows. Expected under the primary: HDPE mcc_peak_hrr_Wg 942 > 748.4 and mcc_total_hr_kJg 45.67 > 42.48 (exp074 training); HDPE mcc_peak_hrr_Wg 942 > 748.4 and mcc_hrc_JgK 1884 > 1496.8 (exp119 training; its mcc_total_hr_kJg max is 49.87, so 45.67 is inside); no exp046 input outside its training range (log_dT 5.71-6.06 vs 5.08-6.10). Tree models saturate beyond their range.
features.freeze: Write features.json (every per-test input row for every variant, the card values used and the gate results) and its sha256 to the log before any label key or series CSV is read.

gates.when: Step 2, label-free, before any prediction. This is the analogue of A2's PS check plus its sanity gates. cone-db has no reference polymer measured by several MCC labs (no PS run; the PMMA-MaCFP MCC block is empty), so A2's same-material +-10% check cannot be built. The blocking gates test instead the two assumptions the rate rule depends on, plus input ranges.
gates.G1_rate_label: For each of the 6 cards: HRC / ('Peak HRR (W/g)' / beta_nominal) must lie in [0.95, 1.05], with beta_nominal = r/60 K/s from the block name. This confirms the block name gives the heating rate HRC was computed with. Drafting look: 0.9915-0.9943. Any failure -> BLOCKED (whole item).
gates.G2_residue_unit: For each card with an STA block: |100 x MCC 'Residue Yield (%)' - <ID>_STA_N2_10K_TGA 'Residue Yield (%)'| <= 10 percentage points. This confirms the MCC field is a fraction. Any failure -> BLOCKED (whole item).
gates.G3_ranges: Per test: Surface Area 0.0095-0.0105 m2; thickness 4-10 mm; density 800-2200 kg/m3; mass/area 3-20 kg/m2; heat flux exactly 50; 'Heat of Combustion O2 (MJ/kg)' 12.5-13.5. Intra-material: each test's density within +-10% of its material's median. Per card: HRC 100-2500 J/gK; primary peak 30-1300 W/g; h_c 3-50 kJ/g; T_peak 350-550 C; T_onset 250-500 C; char yield 0-80%; S2 |Tp' - Tp| <= 40 K. Any failure -> BLOCKED with the values.
gates.reference_context_report_only: A report-only table, never a gate and never a factor. For each card: NIST HRC next to FSRI 30 K/min hrc (ABS 596.7, HDPE 1496.8, FRP_Panel 206.2 at 41.9% char) and FAA AR-05/14 Table A-6 HRC at 1 K/s (ABS 669, PE 1560, PBT 474 at char 0.07, POM 398 neat). Organic-normalised HRC/(1 - r) is shown beside each, with r the MCC residue fraction. Plus h_c and the temperatures. Different products, so this is context only.

models.pHRR_exp074: models/v2/phrr_hgb_v4.joblib (TransformedTargetRegressor(HGB lr 0.05, max_iter 200, max_leaf_nodes 15, min_samples_leaf 10, random_state 0; log1p/expm1), fit on all 191 FSRI rows). Assert that its feature list equals exp074_columns. A refit on train_blend_round1.data_phrr()'s 191 rows must match its predictions on those rows within 1e-6 kW/m2, else BLOCKED (pHRR only). Predictions use the saved joblib.
models.TTI_exp046: make_pipeline(SimpleImputer(median, add_indicator=True), StandardScaler(), PoissonRegressor(alpha=0.01, max_iter=3000)) on v5.PHYS; raw-seconds target; fit on all 681 rows of train_tti_v5_physics --onset-bc --replicate-table (train_blend_round1.data_tti()).
models.FIGRA_exp119: Blend b1 exactly as train_blend_round1.py: Avg([HistGradientBoostingRegressor(max_iter=300, learning_rate=0.05, max_leaf_nodes=15, min_samples_leaf=5, random_state=0), ExtraTreesRegressor(n_estimators=500, min_samples_leaf=2, random_state=0, n_jobs=-1), make_pipeline(SimpleImputer(median, add_indicator=True, keep_empty_features=True), StandardScaler(), Ridge(alpha=10.0))]). The whole Avg is fit on log1p(y) and predictions are expm1, as eval_protocol._fit_predict with log_target=True. Fit on all 197 rows / 67 materials of train_blend_round1.data_figra().
models.step1_reproduce: On FSRI only, before any cone-db prediction: exp074 0.6113 [0.5155, 0.8376] (64 groups, PlasticC -> HIPS), exp046 0.3133 [0.0715, 0.4958] (76 material groups) and exp119 0.4975 [0.3464, 0.6475] (67 material groups, log_target=True) must each reproduce within 0.002 on the mean and both CI ends (repeated GKF 5x10, repeat-0 material bootstrap CI), using the train_blend_round1.py data functions: exp074 and exp046 are its 'exp' candidates for pHRR and TTI, and exp119 is its 'b1' candidate for FIGRA, Avg([data_figra()['inc'], et(), ridge()]) with log_target=True. (Skeptic fix: FIGRA's 'exp' candidate in that script is the old incumbent exp073, ref 0.4563, not exp119.) Otherwise that target is BLOCKED and the others continue.
models.environment: python 3.12.4, scikit-learn 1.7.1, numpy 2.2.6, pandas 2.3.3, scipy 1.16.1 (as for the records). Run with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1.

variants.primary: R1 rate rule (HRC x 0.5; temperatures native), G1 per-test geometry, log_kpc NaN
variants.S1: primary but no rate rescaling (card values as reported)
variants.S2: primary but the single-step/KAS correction (peak, HRC and both temperatures)
variants.rule: Each secondary changes one thing from the primary, on the same rows, in its own column. None is ever primary, compared for selection, or quoted without its label. Secondaries are not crossed.
variants.reporting: For S1-S3 and each target: the headline metrics (R2 only where the min-n rule allows, plus MAE, bias and log R2) and the per-MCC-rate-stratum MAE and bias. No per-material tables for secondaries; their per-test predictions are columns in tests.csv.

labels.series: Exp-Data_Prepared-Final/FTT-White/<Testname>.csv. NIST has already shifted 'Time (s)' so that t = 0 is the FTT 'Test start time' (README; Parse_Cone-FTT.process_data). This is treated as specimen exposure, the FSRI clock (assumed, not verified). HRRPUA(t) = 'HRR (kW)' / 'Surface Area (m2)', from finite rows, with no smoothing or resampling. Sampling is 1 s (FSRI: 0.25 s), which can lower a sharp raw max.
labels.pHRR_obs: Max of HRRPUA over rows with Time >= t_ign (metadata 't_ignition (s)'), mirroring the FSRI replicate table's [TTI, end] window. For GPO3 R2 (operator-invalidated t_ign) the window is Time >= 0, flagged 'window_t0'. NIST gives no end-of-test time ('Test End Time (s)' is null), so the window runs to the last row.
labels.TTI_obs: Metadata 't_ignition (s)' as reported (FTT operator; seconds from test start). No time-zero correction.
labels.FIGRA_obs: pHRR_obs / t_pHRR, with t_pHRR the Time (s) of that maximum (first occurrence) from test start, as ingest_fsri_figra (pHRR / t_pHRR, clock from exposure). The banned max(HRR(t)/t) is not computed.
labels.integrity_report_only: Per test: |pHRR_obs - metadata 'Peak HRRPUA (kW/m2)'| / metadata (NIST's max over the whole series; flagged if > 1%); the max over Time >= 0 vs over Time >= t_ign (flagged if they differ); t_pHRR - t_ign; the NIST '... Outlier' flags. None of these changes a label, a row set or the primary.

scoring.unit: Per test (primary), mirroring A2. The FSRI records' targets are replicate means for pHRR and FIGRA and per-replicate for TTI. Per-material means appear only in the per-material table.
scoring.pools: pHRR: 11 tests / 6 materials (all minus PBT R3). TTI: 11 / 6 (all minus GPO3 R2). FIGRA: 11 / 6 (all minus PBT R3). One flux: 50 kW/m2.
scoring.min_n_rule: R2 (with CI and leave-one-material-out range) is reported for a pool only if it has >= 5 distinct materials AND >= 10 tests. Below that, only n, MAE, bias, mean(obs)/mean(pred) and per-test errors are reported. Pools below the threshold, expected: each MCC-rate stratum (10 K/min: 2 tests / 2 materials; 60 K/min: 9 / 4), the class-overlap and new-class splits, every single material, and the 6 per-material means. Rationale: at one flux, R2 measures only how materials rank against each other; with fewer than 5 materials one material contrast dominates. The rule was set knowing the counts (see prior_looks).
scoring.headline_per_target: R2 in raw units (pHRR kW/m2; TTI seconds, exp046's record metric; FIGRA kW/m2/s), sklearn r2_score. Material-cluster bootstrap 95% CI: eval_protocol.bootstrap_ci(y, pred, groups = 'Material ID', n_boot = 2000, seed = 0), always labelled 'k = 6 clusters, percentile bootstrap undercovers; indicative only'. Bootstrap degeneracy: a draw with fewer than 2 rows gives a non-finite R2. At seed 0 with these 6 groups no such draw occurs (checked from the group IDs alone: 0 single-material draws; 1 of 2000 draws holds only ABS and HDPE, i.e. 6 rows of 2 materials). If one occurs anyway, the CI is reported as 'not computable'. It is never re-seeded and draws are never dropped. Also the leave-one-material-out R2 range (min and max over the 6 drops; r2_score of the frozen predictions on the pool minus one material, with no refit); MAE; bias (mean pred - obs); mean(obs)/mean(pred); log-space R2 (r2_score on log(obs) vs log(pred); rows with a non-positive pred or obs are counted and skipped). TTI adds median |pred - obs|/obs.
scoring.groups: 'Material ID' (6 groups). GPO1 and GPO3 are separate groups: distinct cards, trade names (Glastic vs Redboard) and formulations (GPO3 is the flame-resistant grade).
scoring.per_flux_table: One row (50 kW/m2): n, mean obs, mean pred, MAE, bias, per target. Declared for completeness; a flux response cannot be tested here.
scoring.per_material_table: Per material and target: n, mean obs, mean pred, MAE, bias, mean(obs)/mean(pred), MCC rate, class label (known class, different product / related class / new class), extrapolation flags, comment flags (desiccated, window_t0).
scoring.strata_separate: MCC rate (10 vs 60 K/min) and class label (known class, different product / related class / new class): n, MAE, bias, mean(obs)/mean(pred). Never R2 (min-n rule).
scoring.context_rows_no_model: FSRI ABS and HDPE replicate-mean pHRR and mean TTI at 50 kW/m2 (cone_replicates_fsri.csv), next to the NIST ABS and HDPE observations, labelled 'different product: FSRI 3 mm sheets vs NIST 6 mm; no model'.
scoring.rounding: R2 to 4 decimals; kW/m2, seconds and kW/m2/s to 1 decimal (FIGRA to 2)
scoring.selection_and_adoption: None. Nothing here is a candidate, there is no incumbent comparison, and nothing is promoted.

procedure: 0. Pin check. Enumerate the population by the mcc_card_rule; apply the duplicate rule and the declared test exclusions (asserting the comment phrases); check counts against population.expected and scoring.pools. Any mismatch -> BLOCKED with per-material counts. Only whitelisted metadata keys are read.
1. Reproduce exp074, exp046 and exp119 on FSRI (models.step1_reproduce). Fit the three frozen models (exp074 from the joblib, with its refit check).
2. Gates G1-G3 (label-free); write gates.json with the reference context table.
3. Derive and freeze every input for primary, S1, S2 and S3; extrapolation flags; write features.json and its sha256 to the log. No label key or series CSV has been read yet.
4. Predict every variant for every row; write predictions.csv (no label columns) and its sha256.
5. Read the labels (series CSVs; metadata t_ignition (s), Peak HRRPUA and the '... Outlier' flags for the integrity report only). Compute every metric and table; write tests.csv and summary.json.
6. Fresh-context critic pass before any number is quoted in STATUS, a model card or the scoreboard.

outputs.script: data/v2/validate_external_ftt_white.py (not written in this draft step)
outputs.files: experiments/runs/external_nist_ftt_white/{gates.json, features.json, predictions.csv, tests.csv, summary.json}. tests.csv has one row per test: Testname, Material ID, replicate, MCC rate, class label, flux, m0, thickness, surface area, density, mass/area, test-exclusion flags, comment flags (digits masked), obs pHRR, pred pHRR [primary, S1, S2, S3], obs TTI, pred TTI [primary, S1, S2, S3], obs FIGRA, t_pHRR, pred FIGRA [primary, S1, S2, S3], integrity columns. Written with the csv module or pandas. Optional: reports/external_nist_ftt_white.md (generated tables only). The predictions.csv and features.json sha256 values prove the pre-label freeze. predictions.csv is not bit-reproducible on a rerun: exp119's ExtraTrees uses n_jobs=-1, and the summation order moves values by about 1e-14 (seen in A2).
outputs.tracker: Not ingested. scripts/update_trackers.py reads only top-level experiments/results/*.json and labels rows 'rkf_mean (rgkf5x10)', which would mislabel an external single-lab R2. Any leaderboard or scoreboard mention is the orchestrator's decision after the critic.

interpretation: One lab, one flux, 6 materials (ABS and HDPE have one test each). R2 here measures only how 6 polymers rank against each other at 50 kW/m2. It is not comparable with the FSRI repeated-GKF numbers, which span 15-100 kW/m2 and get much of their variance from flux. The per-test and per-material tables are the result. Quote R2 only together with them and with the LOMO range.
Quote as 'external check, NIST FTT-White 2024 polymers (6 materials, one lab, 50 kW/m2), report-only'. Never SOTA, a win or 'validated'.
The heating-rate rule is a researcher choice, declared before scoring from single-step pyrolysis physics. S1 and S2 show how much it matters; neither may replace the primary after the fact.

The products differ from FSRI's (6 mm sheets from other suppliers vs FSRI's 2-3 mm sheets). Glass-filled composites (GPO1, GPO3, POM-GF) have a thin FSRI analogue (FRP_Panel). PBT's nearest FSRI relatives are PET and PETG. The HDPE inputs lie outside exp074's training range.

Not harmonised: NIST's MCC onset and integration algorithms (undocumented at the pin; the onset-to-peak gaps suggest NIST's onset sits later than FSRI's 5%-of-heat onset, which would bias predicted TTI long); the HRR equation (NIST: full O2/CO2/CO with an ambient-humidity correction, cone-db scripts/utils.calculate_HRR via Parse_Cone-FTT.py; FSRI pHRR: recomputed O2-only, ingest_fsri_figra.hrrpua_curve); TTI by operator button at both labs; t = 0 is FTT 'Test start time'; 1 s sampling vs FSRI 0.25 s; NIST mounting (no frame, no grid, Kaowool blanket, foil pan, 25 mm gap). PBT R3 was desiccated more than 24 h.
The exp054 PMMA cross-lab and A2 MaCFP results are different populations and models. Show them side by side only with labels, never pooled.

exit_and_flag.BLOCKED_or_FLAG: Pin mismatch; population or pool count mismatch; a missing series file; a declared comment phrase not found; a duplicate-rule hit that changes the counts; gate G1, G2 or G3 failure; exp074 joblib feature mismatch or refit mismatch (pHRR only); step-1 reproduction failure (that target only). Write status 'blocked' and the reason in summary.json; the orchestrator writes a blocker file per the exit protocol.
exit_and_flag.EXIT_5: Not applicable: nothing here is compared with a bar, and no number of record can change.

open_choices_resolved: The rate rule: primary R1 (HRC x 0.5 K/s, temperatures native). S1 (no rescaling, by rate stratum) and S2 (single-step/KAS) are report-only. No PS anchor exists in cone-db, so A2's PS-ratio approach cannot be used.
MCC 'Residue Yield (%)' is read as a fraction (x100), checked by gate G2 against STA.
NIST 'T_Onset (K)' fills mcc_t_onset_C despite the undocumented definition. This is disclosed; no onset-NaN variant was added, to keep the variants to one change each.

PBT R3 is out of pHRR and FIGRA (gas pump off) but in TTI. GPO3 R2 is out of TTI (operator-invalidated t_ign) but in pHRR and FIGRA with a t = 0 window. Both rules come from operator comments read with digits masked, before any label.
FIGRA is scorable: every exp119 input (including mcc_hrc_JgK) is on the NIST card, and the label comes from the series.
data/reviewed and Box contribute no rows (no MCC cards). The 2024 FTT-White tests sit in Metadata/Prepared-Final/FTT-White, not in data/reviewed.
Class overlaps (ABS, HDPE, GPO vs FRP_Panel) are not duplicates (different products and thicknesses). They are kept and labelled. The JH_NIJ set is not in this source.
Outputs go to experiments/runs/external_nist_ftt_white/, as the A2 executor did, because experiments/results/ is off-limits to workers here.
Groups = Material ID (6). The bootstrap CI is reported but labelled indicative (k = 6).
